rationale: The six-edge face circulation is a nonzero element of the classified homogeneous boundary kernel.
from_quote: On a honeycomb mesh of side length delta, choose a complete interior hexagonal face with counterclockwise vertices v_0,...,v_5. The complex midpoint field H((v_j+v_{j+1})/2)=delta/(v_{j+1}-v_j), with indices modulo 6 and H=0 elsewhere, satisfies every vertex relation sum_p(p-v)H(p)=0, has six support points of modulus 1, and vanishes at every boundary midpoint. Adding H to a solution preserves every boundary value. This is an author-proved auxiliary result, pending full independent review.
to_quote: Let V be a finite honeycomb vertex set, E the edges with both endpoints in V, H the boundary mid-edges with exactly one endpoint in V, and c the number of components of (V,E). Prescribe complex g on H and b_v=sum_{h in H incident to v}(h-v)g(h). Arbitrary complex interior midpoint values F satisfying sum_{p adjacent to v}(p-v)F(p)=0 exist iff sum_{v in C}b_v=0 on every component C. If solvable, their complex affine dimension is |E|-|V|+c. For a connected plane graph this equals the number of bounded faces. This is an author-proved auxiliary result, pending full independent review.

rationale: Adding the explicitly proved six-edge field to the constant field gives the persistent unit oscillation.
from_quote: There exist simply connected honeycomb patches tending to a fixed hexagonal domain, with mesh delta_n tending to zero, and arbitrary complex midpoint fields F_n with full boundary trace identically 1, sup norm at most 2, and sum_{p adjacent to v}(p-v)F_n(p)=0 at every vertex, but no subsequence converges locally uniformly to a continuous function near a fixed interior point. One may take F_n=1+H_delta_n on a central face; two midpoints at distance sqrt(3)delta_n/2 have value difference of modulus 1. These fields are not asserted to be SAW observables. This is an author-proved auxiliary result, pending full independent review.

to_quote: Proposed observable compactness bridge (false for arbitrary complex midpoint fields): on honeycomb domains with mesh tending to zero, the vertex relation sum_{p adjacent to v}(p-v)F(p)=0, a uniform sup bound, and a fixed full boundary trace would force a locally uniform continuous holomorphic subsequential limit. This proposed implication needs extra hypotheses excluding lattice cycle modes. Its failure does not refute SAW-to-SLE convergence.

rationale: Rank-nullity and the exact face count prove the necessary number of extra independent linear conditions.
from_quote: For a connected finite plane honeycomb graph with f bounded faces and compatible prescribed boundary midpoint values, the homogeneous vertex-relation kernel has complex dimension f. Fewer than f additional complex linear conditions cannot determine interior midpoint values uniquely. Exactly f suffice: orient each internal edge, put J_e=(v-u)F(p_e)/2, and impose c_i^T J=0 on the real signed cycle vectors of the bounded faces. These constraints give a unique solution to the algebraic boundary problem; they are not claimed to hold for the actual SAW observable or to prove a scaling limit. This is an author-proved auxiliary result, pending full independent review.
